review.verdict: Correct casting and a workable split-scene concept are undercut by real rendering bugs — the EXEMPT label is clipped mid-word, the fence is nearly invisible behind the robot, the paper floats disconnected from the hand, and two elements spill outside the safe area — so it reads as cluttered and unclear rather than publish-ready.
revisionNotes: Fence1 is nearly invisible: scale it up to ~1.0 and move to x≈0.28, y≈0.70 so it sits in front of/beside robot1 instead of hidden behind its legs.
The EXEMPT label is clipped to 'EXEM' by robot1's body — scale robot1 down to ~0.75 or shift it right so fence-label has clear space and reads in full.

Paper1 reads as a random floating rectangle in the sky, disconnected from human1's raised hand — reattach it directly to the hand (side 'right' at hand height, not 'top' above the head) so it looks held.

Robot2 almost entirely covers judge1, killing the gavel handoff beat — scale robot2 down to ~0.85 and shift it to x≈0.75 so judge1 stays visible and the gavel bridges the two figures instead of poking out past robot2's far side.
Lint flags human1 and robot2 extending outside the safe area in the final frame — pull human1 right and robot2 left/down so no cast member clips the artboard edge.

review.verdict: The EXEMPT fence half reads clearly, but the court half doesn't: the gavel is hidden behind the robot and there's no bench, so "AI deciding court cases" never lands, and the promised divider line is missing, leaving an unbalanced, dead-space-heavy composition. Fails — needs the gavel/bench fixed and the layout rebalanced before publishing.
revisionNotes: Add the missing courthouse bench in the bottom vignette — the brief calls for the judge standing beside a bench with the robot taking the seat, but no bench shape exists, so the court setting is illegible.

The gavel (gavel1) is almost entirely hidden behind robot2's body — reposition it clear of the robot's torso and bump scale to ~0.9 so the handoff gesture reads; right now there is no visible gavel at all.
Add the thin vertical divider line called for in the brief (or a horizontal rule) to separate the EXEMPT scene from the court scene; without it the two vignettes blend into one cluttered composition.
Composition is top-heavy and left-heavy — the bottom-right quadrant is empty blue grid. Shift the judge/robot group right toward x=0.6-0.65 to balance mass across the square.
Pair the court vignette with a short label (e.g. 'COURT') the way the fence has 'EXEMPT', so both halves announce their scene at the same glance speed.
Robot1's arm lies flat along the fence's top rail instead of reaching over it — rotate the arm further so it visibly reaches toward the person, not just rests on the fence.

revisionNotes: Fix robot1: it's rotated -16° and tipped into fence1's bars, reading as falling over rather than reaching toward the person — zero the rotation and lift it clear of the fence top rail.
The bench-label 'COURT' is partly hidden behind robot2's head/antenna (reads 'C_URT') — raise the label or scale robot2 down slightly so the text clears it.
Per lint, human1 and robot2 extend outside the safe area (human1 x26-277/y566-907, robot2 x690-1078/y542-907) — scale both to ~0.7 and nudge human1 right / robot2 left to clear the margins.
Paper1 floats disconnected above human1's cheering pose instead of being held — switch human1's pose from 'cheer' to a raised-hand/present pose so the paper reads as held up.
Gavel1's long diagonal bar between judge1 and robot2 is ambiguous, almost reading as an extra limb — shorten it and angle it more horizontally for a clearer hand-to-hand pass.
